explanation: Iron in the clay gives it a warm orange-brown colour. The Nok culture of present-day Nigeria made striking terracotta heads more than 2,000 years ago.

claims.text: Terracotta, from the Italian for 'baked earth', is fired clay used for sculpture, pottery and tiles.
Stucco, plaster of Paris and papier-mâché are not fired clay.
Iron compounds in the clay give terracotta its orange-brown colour.
The Nok culture, in present-day Nigeria, made terracotta sculptures, including heads, more than 2,000 years ago.
